title: Free Vibrations and Damping
short: Underdamped, critically damped and overdamped springs.

blocks.html: A mass $m$ on a spring with stiffness $k$, slowed by a damper with coefficient $c$, is the standard example of a second-order equation. The complex roots and repeated roots you have studied are exactly the different ways it can move.

$mx'' + cx' + kx = 0$, with characteristic roots $r = \frac{-c \pm \sqrt{c^{2} - 4mk}}{2m}$.
Undamped ($c = 0$): $x = R\cos(\omega_0t - \delta)$ with natural frequency $\omega_0 = \sqrt{k/m}$ and period $\frac{2\pi}{\omega_0}$.
$c^{2} < 4mk$: underdamped (oscillates with shrinking amplitude); $c^{2} = 4mk$: critically damped; $c^{2} > 4mk$: overdamped (returns without oscillating).

Measure $x$ from the equilibrium position. The spring pulls back with force $-kx$ (Hooke's law) and the damper resists motion with force $-cx'$, so Newton's law $mx'' = -kx - cx'$ gives the equation. The sign of the discriminant $c^{2} - 4mk$ decides whether the roots are complex, repeated or real. For the undamped case, $c_1\cos\omega_0t + c_2\sin\omega_0t$ $= R\cos(\omega_0t - \delta)$ with $R = \sqrt{c_1^{2} + c_2^{2}}$: expand $\cos(\omega_0t - \delta)$ and match coefficients.

blocks.title: An undamped spring
blocks.q: A 0.5 kg mass stretches a spring 0.098 m at rest ($g = 9.8$ m/s²). It is pulled to $x(0) = 0.2$ m and given $x'(0) = 1$ m/s. Find $x(t)$, the amplitude and the period.

blocks.title: A decaying oscillation
blocks.a: $x = e^{-t}\left(\cos 3t + \frac{1}{3}\sin 3t\right)$: it swings with angular frequency 3 inside the envelope $e^{-t}$

blocks.html: Comparing $c$ with $4mk$ instead of $c^{2}$ with $4mk$ (equivalently, $c$ with $2\sqrt{mk}$). Another slip is giving the natural frequency as $\frac{k}{m}$ or $\sqrt{km}$; check units: $\sqrt{k/m}$ has units $\sqrt{(\text{N/m})/\text{kg}} = 1/\text{s}$.

blocks.name: springmass
blocks.cap: A damped spring. Slide the damping $c$ from 0 up past $2\sqrt{mk}$ and watch the motion change from endless bouncing, to shrinking swings, to a slow creep back with no overshoot.
